lessons.title: Starting a dough
lessons.objective: Say what raises a dough, and read a simple order.

cards.prompt: A dough needs flour, water, salt and something to raise it. A `levain` is a culture of flour and water that a baker keeps and feeds for weeks; a poolish is mixed once, the night before, with a little yeast. Either one makes a loaf taste of more than flour.
Which of these is kept and fed for weeks?

options.feedback: A levain is fed again and again, so it lasts.
A poolish is mixed once, for one bake, and used up.
Brine is salted water; it raises nothing.

cards.feedback: A kept culture is what makes a levain a levain.
cards.authorNote: An unknown field, kept as read.

cards.prompt: Shaping a round loaf takes three moves. Fold the edges into the middle. Turn the dough over, seam down. Then pull it across the bench towards you, so the surface tightens.
A culture fed `1:1` flour to water by weight is at ___ hydration.
cards.feedback: Hydration is water over flour: equal weights make 100%.

cards.prompt: Match each word to what it names.
cards.feedback: Two ways to raise a dough, and one tool to hold it while it rises.

cards.prompt: Which of these can raise a dough? Choose every one that can.
cards.feedback: Levain, yeast and poolish all carry live yeast. Salt slows it down; rye flour feeds it but raises nothing on its own.

cards.prompt: Put the steps of a simple loaf in order.
cards.feedback: Mix, rest, shape, bake: the dough needs its rest before it can hold a shape.

cards.prompt: A bakery mixes its dough at six in the evening and wants loaves on the shelf by seven the next morning. The kitchen is cool overnight, the levain was fed at noon, and the oven takes forty minutes to heat. Which plan gets the loaves out on time without rushing the rise or leaving the dough to over-prove before it goes in?

options.text: Shape at five, prove the loaves in the cool kitchen until six, and heat the oven from twenty past five
options.feedback: The rise gets its hour, and the oven is hot when the loaves are ready.

options.text: Shape at midnight and leave the loaves out on the bench all night, then bake them first thing at six
options.feedback: Six hours on the bench is far too long; the loaves collapse before they bake.

options.text: Mix again at four in the morning with extra packet yeast, then shape, prove and bake in one hurried run
options.feedback: Starting again throws away the overnight flavour and rushes every step.

options.text: Bake the dough unshaped at six in the evening and slice the loaves for the shelf on the following morning
options.feedback: Unshaped, unrisen dough bakes into a flat, dense slab.

cards.feedback: Work back from the shelf time: bake, then prove, then shape, with the oven started early enough to be hot.

cards.prompt: Which of these slows a levain down when it goes into the dough?

options.feedback: Salt tightens the dough and slows the culture.

cards.feedback: Bakers add salt after the first mix for this reason.

cards.prompt: A customer leaves this note at the counter. What do they want?

artifact.text:
2 x round sourdough
Sat, ready by 08:00
sliced pls, no seeds

options.text: Two round sourdough loaves, sliced, without seeds, by eight on Saturday
options.feedback: Everything the note asks for, read in full.

options.text: Two seeded round loaves, left whole, ready on Saturday morning
options.feedback: The note says no seeds, and asks for the loaves sliced.

options.text: Round sourdough for two people, with seeds, on Saturday
options.feedback: "2 x" counts loaves, not people, and the note rules out seeds.

lessons.title: At the oven
lessons.objective: Read the signs of a good bake, and name the tools around the oven.

verification.note: Invented content, marked for review to test the marker.

cards.prompt: `Oven spring` is the last rise a loaf makes in the first minutes of baking, before the crust sets. A deep score gives that rise somewhere to go: the cut opens and lifts into a flap called the ear.
Tap the ear: the flap a good score lifts as the loaf springs.

regions.label: The ear
regions.feedback: The ear is the edge of the cut, lifted by oven spring.

regions.label: A large air pocket
regions.feedback: A large pocket is trapped gas, often from loose shaping.

regions.label: The crumb
regions.feedback: The crumb is the inside; the ear is on the crust.

regions.label: The base
regions.feedback: The base sat on the oven floor; nothing lifts there.

cards.feedback: A clean, lifted ear shows the score was deep enough and the loaf still had spring in it.

cards.prompt: Match each tool to its job.
cards.feedback: Four tools, four jobs, from the bench to the oven.

cards.prompt: The recipe says to make a poolish tonight. What do you mix?

options.text: Flour, water and a little packet yeast
options.feedback: That is a poolish: mixed once, used in the morning.

options.text: A spoonful of the kept levain, fed again
options.feedback: That feeds a levain; it doesn't make a poolish.

options.text: Flour and water alone, left for a week
options.feedback: That starts a new culture, which takes days.

cards.feedback: Poolish: one night, a little yeast.
cards.trapFeedback: A poolish and a levain both raise dough, but one is mixed for a single bake and the other is kept. Swapping them changes the timing of the whole bake.

cards.prompt: Which of these names mean the same tool?

options.note: A linen cloth for long loaves, not a basket.
A warm cabinet, not a basket.

cards.feedback: A banneton goes by several names; all of them mean the basket.
cards.trapFeedback: A couche shapes long loaves in cloth; a banneton is a basket for round ones. Ordering the wrong one brings the wrong tool to the bench.

cards.prompt: The night baker leaves this handover. Which batch needs attention first?

artifact.text:
Batch 3: under-proved, in the fridge since 03:00
Batch 4: shaped 05:10, proving at room heat
Oven: at heat since 05:30

options.text: Batch 4, proving warm and nearest its peak
options.feedback: Room heat moves fastest; it peaks before the cold batch does.
The fridge slows it right down; it can wait.

options.text: The oven, because it has been on too long
options.feedback: An oven at heat is ready, not at risk.
